cards.text: This psalm doesn't say who wrote it, but it opens with a call: 'Sing to the LORD a new song.' Not the same old tune on repeat, friend. A brand NEW one!

cards.question: The psalm calls for a new song to the LORD. What reason does it give?

cards.text: The psalm also talks about a victory. And it is VERY clear about who won it.

cards.question: True or false: The psalm says Israel's army gained the LORD the victory.

cards.text: His own right hand and holy arm gained Him the victory. My mustache has packed a LOT of cookie boxes, friend, but it has never won anything bigger than a staring contest with the oven.

cards.question: The psalm goes on: the LORD has ___ His salvation and revealed His righteousness to the nations.

cards.text: Then the psalm looks at Israel. He has remembered His love and faithfulness to the house of Israel, and friend, He remembers a whole lot better than I remember an oven timer.

cards.question: True or false: The psalm says only the house of Israel has seen the salvation of our God.

cards.text: Now the psalm turns a corner. It's done telling what the LORD did, and it starts handing out invitations.

cards.question: The psalm starts calling for praise to the LORD. Who is it calling on?
True or false: The psalm wants this praise to the LORD kept soft and quiet.

cards.text: A joyful NOISE, friend, not a perfect one, which is GREAT news for my singing voice. Then the psalm brings in the band, starting with the lyre and the harp.

cards.question: After the lyre and the harp, the psalm turns the volume UP. What joins in next?
The psalm calls everyone to shout for joy before the LORD, the King. True or false: It calls on more than people, and invites the sea and all that fills it too.

cards.text: Then the psalm says, 'Let the rivers clap their hands.' Friend, I clap with a MUSTACHE, and even I'm impressed.

cards.question: The rivers aren't the only part of creation the psalm calls on. What else does it call to sing together for joy?
The psalm calls the rivers and the mountains to rejoice before the LORD, the King. What reason does it give?

answers.text: He comes to judge the earth
He sends rain on the land
He made them by His hand

cards.text: Judgment might sound like the scary part. But this psalm calls all of creation to rejoice about it, and I think it's because of HOW He judges.

cards.question: How will the LORD judge the world? With ___.

cards.text: And the peoples? He judges them with equity. Fair all the way around, friend, and THAT is worth some river applause.

findings.problem: This fill in the blank asks the baker to guess the last words of the line "He will judge the world with ___" from three abstract nouns: righteousness, power and mercy. It is the same pattern as the bad Psalm 23 example ("He guides me in the paths of…" with righteousness, peace or ancient). Card 18 says creation rejoices because of HOW He judges, which makes "mercy" just as reasonable a pick as "righteousness", so the card comes down to luck. It should ask about the meaning instead, for example whether His judging is something to fear or to celebrate, and why.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank tests the wording of the line, not meaning the baker can reason out. After card 18's setup, "mercy" fits as well as "righteousness".

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This is the second joke built on the mustache (card 5 was "My mustache has packed a LOT of cookie boxes…"). It makes up a large share of the walkthrough's few jokes. The punchline "even I'm impressed" also doesn't land right away, because it isn't clear what he is impressed by.

rule.text: The mustache is a fact about him, not his main source of jokes.

findings.problem: The joke's logic is unclear. It isn't obvious whether "even I'm impressed" means he is impressed by the rivers or by himself, so a baker has to stop and work it out.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: Most of the humor reads as pleasant rather than laugh-out-loud. Card 1 ("Not the same old tune on repeat, friend. A brand NEW one!"), card 7 (oven timer) and card 20 ("worth some river applause") are mild. Big moments such as the rivers clapping, the mountains singing and the whole earth called to make noise never get a real comic build.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
